cards.headline: John Dramani Mahama arrives in Egypt for AU summit and Alamein Africa Forum

cards.headline: Megapoll finds nearly half of UK voters support rejoining EU

pages.text: A poll by the Messina Group (TMG) found that almost half of all voters support Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s preference to rejoin the European Union after the next election. The findings suggest that renegotiating the UK’s relationship with the EU could increase the Labour Party's vote share by as much as seven points, provided the prime minister offers a fresh referendum and campaigns for re-entry into the bloc. Regarding the decision-making process, almost a third of voters stated an in-out referendum would be required first, while more than one in six believed a general election mandate would be sufficient, and an equal proportion felt parliament could make the decision. On September 29, 2026, Burnham used his first Labour conference speech as leader to announce a review of options for Britain’s future relationship with Europe, noting that these options should include rejoining entirely.

The poll results come amid internal political caution within the Labour government. Two-thirds of cabinet ministers, including Burnham, first secretary Louise Haigh, chancellor John Healey, and foreign secretary Ed Miliband, represent seats that backed Brexit and have previously stated they would respect the 2016 vote. Some Labour MPs have expressed concerns that testing public support for rejoining could pose political risks and potentially benefit Reform. Several ministers have also publicly cautioned against the move: deputy leader Lucy Powell stated going beyond inherited EU reset plans was “not possible nor desirable”; trade secretary Jonathan Reynolds cited “constitutional questions” causing business uncertainty; and home secretary Shabana Mahmood noted that rejoining is “not a simple, straightforward thing” and that costs might be unacceptable.

cards.headline: Magnitude 4.8 earthquake strikes near Leongatha, Victoria

pages.text: Geoscience Australia detected a preliminary magnitude 4.8 earthquake at 2:01 a.m. near Leongatha, located 130km south-east of Melbourne. The quake was estimated to have occurred at a depth of approximately 10km. Tremors were felt across Melbourne's eastern suburbs and other areas including Narre Warren, Garfield, Preston, Heidelberg Heights, and Venus Bay. Geoscience Australia reported receiving thousands of accounts from individuals who felt the earthquake. The Bureau of Meteorology stated there was no tsunami threat resulting from the event. The earthquake occurred in South Gippsland, a region identified as being among the most active seismic zones in Australia. This event was the largest recorded in the state since a magnitude 5.0 earthquake on the Great Ocean Road in 2023. An aftershock with a magnitude of 3.1 was recorded 55 minutes after the initial quake. Additionally, a magnitude 3.3 earthquake was recorded on the morning of October 1, 2026, at Yarram, approximately 80km east of Leongatha.

cards.headline: South Korean President threatens further action over Ukrainian disclosure of North Korean prisoners of war

pages.text: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has threatened to take unspecified further action if Ukraine does not issue a public apology regarding the disclosure that two North Korean prisoners of war were sent to South Korea. The tension follows a disclosure made by Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky to the UN General Assembly last week, which Seoul claims was intended to remain secret. According to Lee's office, Ukraine had requested confidentiality to protect the North Koreans' families and to avoid criticism regarding the potential loss of an opportunity to exchange the soldiers for Ukrainian prisoners of war. However, Zelensky's office responded that no such agreement to maintain confidentiality existed between the two countries. President Lee rejected characterizations of the dispute as a misunderstanding, stating on X that the matter concerns the dignity of the Korean people and the nation. He further accused Kyiv of attempting to provoke a war on the Korean Peninsula, expressing regret that Ukraine is discussing an imminent military clash between the North and South instead of acknowledging the agreement and apologizing. Domestically, Lee has faced criticism from the South Korean opposition, who accused him of covering up the transfer to appease Pyongyang. The two soldiers involved, who were among thousands of North Koreans supporting Russia in the Ukraine war, had previously told local media they wished to be sent to South Korea.

On October 1, 2026, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha described the situation to Ukrainian media as a diplomatic misunderstanding. Sybiha stated that Kyiv is working to resolve the issue, noting that South Korea is an important country and expressing hope for concrete results in the near future. He said, 'We are working on it. cards.headline: FDA inspectors detect cyclospora at Mexican farm linked to lettuce outbreak

pages.text: On October 2, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced that inspectors detected the parasite cyclospora at a Mexican farm in Guanajuato. The agency reported finding the microscopic parasite in a wastewater tank and a drainage ditch used for lettuce cultivation. The FDA stated that while it is unclear how the lettuce became infected, the samples provide “strong epidemiological data” linking the outbreak to the Taylor Farms site. This announcement follows an investigation by the agency that began more than six weeks prior, marking its first visit to the location in over seven years. This outbreak, which the CDC declared ended less than a month before this announcement, infected nearly 13,000 people across 21 states, resulting in 570 hospitalizations and two deaths.

The FDA's findings follow conflicting reports from regulatory bodies. Mexico’s food safety authority previously conducted an investigation and stated that cyclospora was not detected in the water or lettuce at the facility. This followed an instance where the FDA retracted a faulty test result that had incorrectly identified the parasite in a lettuce sample from Taylor Farms collected at the border. In response to the FDA's findings, Taylor Farms attributed the cited contamination to an independent grower who is no longer part of their supplier program. The company stated its facility in central Mexico remains closed while a research team works to implement enhanced safety protocols from the field to the facility.

cards.headline: Saudi Arabia reports Flydubai co-pilot assaulted captain during flight to Tel Aviv

pages.text: Saudi Arabia announced on October 1, 2026, that a Flydubai co-pilot assaulted the captain during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, resulting in an emergency landing in Tabuk. According to the Saudi Interior Ministry, preliminary investigations conducted alongside a UAE security team found that the assault left both pilots with injuries. Flydubai flight FZ1073 departed Dubai International Airport for Ben Gurion International Airport on September 30, 2026, before being granted permission to make an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk. The aircraft landed safely at 9:45 a.m. local time with 174 passengers and eight crew members on board. Following the landing, Saudi authorities provided assistance to those on board. All passengers continued their journey at 5:40 p.m. via a replacement Flydubai aircraft, while the remaining crew returned to Dubai on another airline flight. The captain and co-pilot were hospitalized for treatment; after receiving medical clearance and showing improved conditions, they departed Saudi Arabia for Abu Dhabi on October 1, 2026, accompanied by a UAE security team.

Flydubai previously stated that an altercation occurred inside the cockpit and that crew members secured the aircraft before diverting to Saudi Arabia. The airline noted that the causes and motives behind the incident remain unknown and are subject to an official investigation. The UAE Public Prosecution has ordered an investigation to determine if the incident was linked to terrorist activity or a pre-planned motive. Additionally, Saudi Arabia’s National Transport Safety Center has launched a separate safety investigation to collect evidence and assess aviation safety aspects regarding the incident.

cards.headline: Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia following embassy closure and diplomat expulsion

pages.text: Eritrea announced it was severing all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia on October 1, 2026. The decision by Eritrea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed an announcement from Addis Ababa that it would close its embassy in Asmara and expel 10 Eritrean diplomats. Eritrea stated the move was a reciprocation of Ethiopia's actions, which it described as an “agenda of incessant hostility” involving the infringement on coastal areas and the arming of fighters opposed to the Eritrean government. Both nations have rejected mutual accusations of backing armed groups opposed to their respective governments. Ethiopia has also expelled an Egyptian diplomat, providing 48 hours for departure, though the government has not publicly stated a reason for that decision. Al Jazeera reports that the diplomatic breakdown follows months of worsening relations driven by disputes over Ethiopia's push for Red Sea access and allegations that Eritrea is backing the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival fighting in northern Ethiopia. Ethiopia has further accused Egypt and Sudan of joining Eritrea in supporting Tigrayan rebel forces. Analysts warn that the unrest could potentially destabilize Sudan and spill into neighboring states.

Renewed fighting has emerged in northern Ethiopia between federal troops and an opposition alliance across parts of the Tigray, Afar, and Amhara regions. BBC World reports that more than 50 people have been killed since heavy fighting resumed in northern Ethiopia last week. These clashes are described as the most severe in Ethiopia since the 2020-2022 civil war, which resulted in hundreds of thousands of deaths. The fighting involves Ethiopian federal forces battling fighters from the TPLF and its allies, an alliance that Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea of supporting.

While Netanyahu cited radicalization as a potential clue, he emphasized that final conclusions regarding motive have yet to be made.

Investigations into the motive behind the attack are being conducted by Saudi investigators in cooperation with the United Arab Emirates, the United States, Oman, and Israel. A regional official told the Associated Press that all scenarios, ranging from terrorism to mental disorders, are being examined. The UAE state news agency reported that investigations have begun to determine if the incident was linked to terrorist activity. While two Israeli security officials stated their initial assessment was that the co-pilot was likely acting alone, US President Donald Trump and UAE officials have indicated to the media that Iran may be responsible, though they have not definitively blamed Tehran. On September 23, 2026, Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure, noting that both sides remain far apart on how to end the war. This follows a September 22, 2026, statement from US President Donald Trump, who suggested an agreement could arrive soon but also stated he could 'annihilate' Iran if no deal is reached to end the conflict. The war began on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran, prompting Tehran to respond with strikes on Israel and Gulf states hosting US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have resulted in thousands of deaths and the displacement of millions. President Trump has identified weakening Iran's nuclear capabilities as a war objective. While the US is nuclear-armed, Iran does not possess nuclear weapons and denies seeking them, maintaining it has the right to develop nuclear technology for peaceful purposes as a party to the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

cards.headline: One killed and four injured in explosion at car repair shop in Daraa countryside

pages.text: An unexplained explosion at a car repair shop in Nawa, located in western Syria’s Daraa countryside, killed one person and injured four others, including two children, on Thursday, according to the North Press Agency. A local source reported that the injured individuals were transported to Nawa National Hospital and Daraa National Hospital for medical treatment. The blast also caused damage to several nearby homes and shops, as well as the area's water and electricity networks. While repair crews and relevant authorities worked to restore services, authorities arrived at the site to begin investigating the circumstances and cause of the explosion. As of Thursday, the cause of the blast had not been determined.
